nodes.description: Investigational, not established practice. Exogenous interleukin-2 restored CD25 and interferon-gamma production, and in one patient T cell proliferation, in CARMIL2-deficient cells in vitro, in a dose-dependent manner. The authors propose it should be studied further as a therapeutic modality; no clinical trial has tested it. No `therapeutic_agent` is bound, and the reason is a genuine gap rather than an oversight. The study used generic exogenous interleukin-2, not a named product. NCIT does carry a generic cytokine term (NCIT:C20507 Interleukin-2), but that term is a protein rather than a chemical entity and is not a member of the ChemicalEntityTerm enum this slot binds to; it was tried and rejected by validation. The terms that would validate name specific recombinant products such as aldesleukin, and binding one would assert a specificity the study does not have. No term beats a wrong term, so the slot is left empty.

nodes.description: CARMIL2 is a capping-protein regulator, and the original description of the human disease reported perturbed cytoskeletal organization with T cell polarity and migration defects. evidence.reference_title: Dual T cell- and B cell-intrinsic deficiency in humans with biallelic RLTPR mutations.
evidence.snippet: Their CD4+ T cells exhibit a "Th2" cell bias ex vivo and when cultured in vitro, contrasting with the paucity of "Th1," "Th17," and T follicular helper cells.

nodes.description: Cutaneous control of human papillomavirus and of molluscum contagiosum virus is lost in the keratinocyte compartment, producing warts and molluscum that resist treatment and persist from early childhood. This is the point at which the immunological lesion becomes visible skin disease. This node captures the single concept of failed cutaneous viral control.
nodes.id: Uncontrolled Cutaneous Papillomavirus and Poxvirus Replication

evidence.reference_title: A potential founder variant in CARMIL2/RLTPR in three Norwegian families with warts, molluscum contagiosum, and T-cell dysfunction.
evidence.snippet: Four patients from three Norwegian families presented with a common skin phenotype of warts, molluscum contagiosum, and dermatitis since early childhood, and various other immunological features.

evidence.reference_title: Human CARMIL2 deficiency underlies a broader immunological and clinical phenotype than CD28 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Like CD28-deficient patients, CARMIL2-deficient patients display recalcitrant warts and low blood counts of CD4+ and CD8+ memory T cells and CD4+ TREGs.

nodes.description: Epstein-Barr virus escapes cell-mediated control and drives smooth muscle proliferation, producing EBV-positive smooth muscle tumours - the most distinctive neoplastic complication of this disease and one that has been refractory to conventional treatment. This node captures the single concept of uncontrolled EBV in the smooth muscle compartment.
nodes.id: Uncontrolled EBV Infection of Smooth Muscle

evidence.reference_title: A human immunodeficiency syndrome caused by mutations in CARMIL2.
evidence.snippet: Here, we show four human patients with EBV+ disseminated smooth muscle tumours that carry two homozygous loss-of-function mutations in the CARMIL2 (RLTPR) gene encoding the capping protein regulator and myosin 1 linker 2.

evidence.reference_title: A Novel Pathogenic Variant in CARMIL2 (RLTPR) Causing CARMIL2 Deficiency and EBV-Associated Smooth Muscle Tumors.
evidence.snippet: CARMIL2 deficiency is a rare combined immunodeficiency (CID) characterized by defective CD28-mediated T cell co-stimulation, altered cytoskeletal dynamics, and susceptibility to Epstein Barr Virus smooth muscle tumors (EBV-SMTs).
